annotationRationale: The expected value weights each possible maximum by its probability. Multiplication counting supplies the equally likely placements and their case counts.
sourceMethod: Followed the official enumeration of 27 placements, counting maximums of one and three directly and obtaining the maximum-two count by subtraction.

review.mathCheck: Among 27 equally likely placements, maxima 1 and 3 occur 6 and 3 times. Maximum 2 occurs 3·2·3 = 18 times, choosing the doubled jar, singleton jar, and singleton coin. The expected maximum is (6 + 36 + 9)/27 = 17/9, choice D.
review.sourceMethodCheck: Faithful, originally worded expansion of MAA Problem 16, page 13. It uses the same maximum-occupancy partition, counts 6, 18, and 3, and takes their weighted average.
review.annotationCheck: The explanation justifies equal likelihood, exhausts all maxima, and explains expectation as an average. Tracking coins separately is valid even if the physical coins look identical.
